extracted.intended_audience: general public, policymakers, legal researchers, and practitioners interested in federal rulemaking and unfunded mandates
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) requirements that govern legislative and regulatory processes to limit imposition of unfunded federal mandates on state, local, and tribal governments and to require cost assessments and consultation for costly rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on federal imposition of unfunded mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (UMRA) restricts the federal imposition of unfunded mandates on state, local and tribal governments in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UMRA is intended to curb the practice of imposing unfunded Federal mandates on States and local governments, strengthen the partnership between Federal and subnational governments, and ensure the Federal Government pays costs those governments incur in complying with certain federal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title I — Legislative Accountability and Reform (CBO submission and appropriation requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any bill passed by committee must be submitted to the director of the Congressional Budget Office so that any federal mandates may be identified. No bill which contains any such mandate imposing a direct cost of more than fifty million dollars on a state, local or tribal government or a cost of more than one hundred million dollars on the private sector may be sent to the full chamber without a corresponding appropriation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for legislation: committee-passed bills require CBO identification of mandates; hard cost thresholds ($50M for state/local/tribal; $100M for private sector) bar transmission to the floor absent a corresponding appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title II — Regulatory Accountability and Reform (agency cost assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies must assess the cost of all new regulations to state, local and tribal governments and the private sector before issuing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are required to quantify and consider regulatory costs to subnational governments and private sector entities as part of rulemaking; the assessment is a precondition to issuing new regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title II — Regulatory Accountability and Reform (consultation and less-burdensome alternatives for >$100M rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where such costs exceed one hundred million dollars, the issuing agency must consult with the affected governments and make sure that no less burdensome alternative exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For rules with estimated costs over $100M to governments or the private sector, agencies must engage in consultation with affected state/local/tribal governments and demonstrate consideration (and absence) of less burdensome alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title III — Review of Federal Mandates (advisory review and recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations was directed to review the role of mandates in relations between the federal government and state, local and tribal governments and to recommend to Congress and to the president opportunities to simplify or eliminate federal mandates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandate-review function: an advisory body is to evaluate impacts of mandates and propose simplification or elimination opportunities as policy guidance to Congress and the President.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IV — Judicial Review (enforcement of Title II obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal courts may compel agencies to comply with their responsibilities under Title II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UMRA provides an enforcement mechanism by allowing judicial review to require agencies to follow the statute's regulatory cost-assessment, consultation, and related obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of affected entities
rubrics_metrics.description: UMRA specifically addresses mandates affecting state, local, and tribal governments and the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying UMRA's requirements (cost thresholds, consultation, and CBO review), the relevant potential impacts are measured for those categories of entities; different thresholds and procedural consequences apply depending on whether costs fall on governments or the private sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative intent — ensure federal payment for costs of compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The long title and text articulate an objective 'to ensure that the Federal Government pays the costs incurred by those governments in complying with certain requirements under Federal statutes and regulations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UMRA's purpose informs interpretation: rules or statutes that impose compliance costs on subnational governments without funding run counter to the Act's stated aims and may trigger the Act's procedural protections and constraints.
